sentences.text: Before analyzing any circuit, an engineer must identify its topological elements.
A branch represents any single two-terminal component, such as a resistor or voltage source.
A node is the point of connection between two or more branches.
A loop is any closed path in a circuit formed by starting at a node, passing through elements, and returning to the same node without passing through any node more than once.
A network with b branches, n nodes, and l independent loops satisfies the fundamental topology theorem: b = l + n - 1.
The Fundamental Network Theorem: b = l + n - 1 which means that l = b - n + 1 .
This theorem defines the exact number of independent KCL ( n - 1 ) and KVL ( l ) equations required to solve any network.
Voltage is always a relative measurement between two points.
To simplify circuit schematics, engineers define a common reference node called Ground, assigned a potential of 0 Volts.
All other node voltages are measured with respect to this 0V ground point.
